long_biography.plain_text:
Bank Millennium grew from the commercial bank Bogusław Kott co-founded in 1989 after fourteen years specialising in foreign-trade finance at Poland's Ministry of Finance. A Warsaw School of Economics graduate, he guided its introduction of Poland's first Visa payment card and listing as the first financial institution on the Warsaw Stock Exchange.

The bank absorbed Łódzki Bank Rozwoju and merged with Bank Gdański, creating the universal lender that later adopted the Millennium name. After twenty-four years as chief executive, Kott chaired the supervisory board until March 2025. His wider institutional roles included the Polish Business Roundtable and the board of trustees at Kozminski University.

uncertainties.detail: The uncommon exact full name, birth cohort, nationality, residence and banking history resolve the Bank Millennium co-founder at high confidence. Puls Biznesu independently described him as spending time on his own yacht, but no credible public source identified that yacht as Gatto; vessel details are excluded from both biographies.

The public LinkedIn result for 'Boguslaw Kott MA LL.M' is a younger London-based compliance professional at Bally's Interactive and does not match the 1947-born Polish banker. It was rejected and no facts or social link were transferred.

Several secondary pages identify Wielbark as Kott's birthplace, but no first-party biography or sufficiently authoritative public register located in this review confirms the place. The field remains blank. The birth day is proposed separately from an exact KRS-derived identity record.

Sources positively establish that Kott co-founded and built the bank and personally held shares, but do not characterise his family wealth, networks or financial platform well enough to choose the independent or advantaged subtype. No family ownership or succession is documented; the bank's executive and supervisory transitions are not treated as family transfers.

Historical filings establish Bank Millennium share ownership and business reporting establishes high executive remuneration, but no current shareholding or complete asset schedule was located after Kott left the bank's supervisory board in March 2025. Primary industry therefore uses the disclosed origin-sector fallback, while wealth relationship remains Unknown.

Focused searches across LinkedIn, Instagram, Facebook, X/Twitter, YouTube, TikTok and personal-web results found no account authenticated to the 1947-born Bank Millennium co-founder. The official company website is proposed separately; no personal account is guessed.

Banking is the only approved active tag proposed because it captures Kott's defining long-term operating mandate and wealth sector. Competitive sailing was considered but omitted: public material establishes enthusiasm and historical foundation or financial-committee involvement, not a sufficiently sustained defining professional, competitive, ownership or senior-governance identity under the active tag contract.

The short biography answers identity and wealth origin through founder leadership, shareholding and remuneration. The long profile omits the shares and pay, instead developing Kott's government-finance formation, payment-card and listing milestones, acquisitions, merger and institutional roles. Both remain independent of current vessel ownership.
